title: First access
description: Enter the administrator details and the bootstrap token provided at deployment to create the company's first access.
unavailable: First access could not be completed. Check the data and the token, then try again.
resetDescription: Enter your username. If it exists, we send a code to the registered contact.
resetCodeSent: If the username exists, the code is on its way to the registered contact. It is valid for 15 minutes.
resetRejected: Could not finish the reset. Check the code and the password and try again.
resetDone: Password changed. You can sign in with the new password.

users.title: System users
users.intro: Who signs in to this installation, with which roles, and where the invitation is delivered. Accounts are created disabled: the person receives a code and chooses their own password.
users.empty: No user besides your own account.
users.forbidden: Only accounts that manage users can see this list. Ask a company administrator for the permission.
users.resendSucceeded: Invitation resent. The previous code no longer works.

inviteDialog.title: Invite user
inviteDialog.intro: The account starts disabled and without a password. The activation code is sent through the chosen channel.
inviteDialog.name: Full name
inviteDialog.rolesHint: At least one role. The role decides what the person can see.
inviteDialog.taxIdHint: Optional. With a Driver or Aggregate role, it is what finds the fleet record.
inviteDialog.channelHint: How the activation code is delivered.
inviteDialog.contactField: This is where the invitation goes.

editDialog.title: Edit user
editDialog.name: Full name
editDialog.usernameHint: Lowercase, no spaces or accents; dot, hyphen and underscore are accepted.
editDialog.usernameInvalid: Login outside the accepted format: 3 to 60 characters, starting with a letter or digit.
editDialog.contactHint: The stored contact is masked in the list; fill this only to replace it.
editDialog.contactRequired: Changing the channel requires the matching contact.
editDialog.emailHint: This is the login e-mail. Changing it requires verification again and does not change the invitation channel.
editDialog.rolesHint: The role list is replaced entirely by whatever is checked here.
editDialog.phoneHint: Fill in only to replace the stored phone.
editDialog.taxIdHint: Fill in only to replace the stored tax ID.

realm.title: In the login provider
realm.intro: What Keycloak knows about this person, and which attribute matched the two accounts.
realm.absent: This person has no matching account in the login provider.
realm.noEmail: The provider account has no email.
realm.subject: Provider identifier
realm.fillHint: The local profile is empty. The provider has this account name and email — copying them is done by the server, because the address is masked on this screen.
realm.diverged: The provider and the local record disagree on: {{fields}}. The provider one is what authenticates.

password.title: Password
password.intro: Setting the password here serves people with no working email. Otherwise the reset link is the path where the final password never passes through your hands.
password.label: New password
password.temporary: Require a change on first sign-in
password.temporaryHint: When checked, the person signs in with this password and must choose another right away.
password.resetSent: Request sent. If the login exists and is active, the link arrives through the registered channel.

removeDialog.title: Remove the account
removeDialog.warning: The company membership is dropped and the person loses access to this installation. The history of what they recorded is preserved.

errors.default: The operation could not be completed. Try again.
errors.COMPANY_USERS_FORBIDDEN: Your account does not manage users for this company.
errors.COMPANY_USERS_REQUEST_FAILED: The API did not answer. Check the connection and try again.
errors.COMPANY_USERS_RESPONSE_INVALID: The API answered in an unexpected format.
errors.COMPANY_USER_NOT_FOUND: This user no longer belongs to the company. Refresh the list.
errors.COMPANY_USER_CONTACT_TAKEN: An account with this contact already exists.
errors.IDENTITY_SUBJECT_NOT_FOUND: The account has no identity in the login provider. Invite the person again.
errors.SELF_MEMBERSHIP_REMOVAL: Nobody removes their own account. Ask another administrator.
errors.COMPANY_USER_TAX_ID_TAKEN: An account with this tax id already exists.
errors.USERNAME_CHANGE_REFUSED: The login provider does not allow changing this account username. The rest of the profile was saved; the username is unchanged.
errors.INVALID_REQUEST: A field is not in the accepted format. Check username, email, phone and tax ID.
errors.INTERNAL_ERROR: The API failed to process the request. If it repeats, it is a defect on our side.
errors.USER_PICTURE_TOO_LARGE: The image is over 256 KB. Reduce it and upload again.
errors.USER_PICTURE_UNSUPPORTED_FORMAT: Unsupported format. The picture must be PNG, JPEG or WebP — the server checks the file itself, not the name.

fleetLink.linked: Linked to the existing fleet record.
fleetLink.noDriverRecord: Invitation sent, but no fleet record matches this tax id — create the record so the person shows up in the fleet.

sync.title: Keycloak reconciliation
sync.intro: Who exists here, who exists in the login provider, and who exists on one side only. Divergence never shows in the list above — it shows here.
sync.allLinked: Every account exists on both sides.
sync.truncated: Keycloak holds more accounts than this page fetched — divergence may exist outside it.
sync.missingCount_one: 1 access exists on one side only.
sync.missingCount_other: {{count}} accesses exist on one side only.
sync.profileMissingCount_one: 1 access exists on both sides with no local profile.
sync.profileMissingCount_other: {{count}} accesses exist on both sides with no local profile.

skipReason.realm-contact-missing: the provider account has no email
skipReason.service-account: it is a service account, not a person

sync.outOfSyncCount_one: 1 access exists on both sides with different data.
sync.outOfSyncCount_other: {{count}} accesses exist on both sides with different data.

bulk.selectAll: Select every row on this page
bulk.addsOnly: Roles are added. Whoever already has one keeps it, and nothing is removed.

matrix.title: What each role can see
matrix.intro: The role and permission matrix of this installation. Read-only: changing what a role reaches is a code change, reviewed — this screen exists so granting a role stops being blind.

groups.title: Access groups
groups.intro: A group is the role the company designs: catalog roles plus loose permissions, assigned to many people at once. It adds to what a person already has — it never removes.
groups.name: Group name
groups.rolesOptional: Roles are optional: a group may grant only loose permissions.

permissions.intro: Permissions granted directly to this person, outside any group.
permissions.none: No loose permission. Everything she reaches comes from roles and groups.
permissions.preferGroups: Prefer a group: it explains why the person reaches that, and a loose permission does not.

picture.review: Check before saving. The cutout is a suggestion — the model sometimes eats a detail.
picture.cutoutFailed: Could not remove the background. The original photo still works.

login.title: Sign in
login.intro: Type how you are known in the system. The password is asked on the next screen, at the access provider.
login.label: Email, tax id or phone
login.hint: Any of your registered contacts works.

profiles.title: Roles and groups
profiles.intro: What each catalogue role reaches, the groups the company designs, and who belongs to them. Provider reconciliation stays on the access screen, next to the listing it repairs.

assign.title: Assign a group to people
assign.intro: Pick the group and the people. Assignment adds to what each already has — it never removes — and whoever is already in the group is ignored.
assign.truncated: The list shows the first 100 people. For the rest, use the selection on the access screen.
